---
title: "Self-Adaptation in Continuous Markov Decision Processes"
resources:
  - config.py
  - mdp.py
  - basis.py
  - policy.py
  - helper.py
  - psmd
  - self_guided_alp
format:
  live-revealjs:
    theme: simple
    width: 1600
    height: 900
    margin: 0.055
    center: false
    controls: true
    progress: true
    slide-number: "c/t"
    navigation-mode: linear
    transition: fade
    background-transition: fade
    hash: true
    preview-links: auto
    code-overflow: wrap
    html-math-method: mathjax
    include-in-header:
      text: |
        <script type="text/x-mathjax-config">
        MathJax.Hub.Config({
          "HTML-CSS": {
            availableFonts: ["TeX"],
            preferredFont: "TeX",
            webFont: "TeX",
            imageFont: null
          }
        });
        </script>
pyodide:
  packages:
    - numpy
    - scipy
    - matplotlib
  cell-options:
    completion: true
    persist: false
    startover: true
    timelimit: 180
---

```{pyodide}
#| autorun: true

import time
from types import SimpleNamespace

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

from config import (
    CONTINUOUS_MDP_NOTEBOOK_CONFIG,
    FALPConfig,
    GuidingConstraintConfig,
    HiGHSSolverConfig,
    LowerBoundConfig,
    PolicyEvaluationConfig,
    PSMDConfig,
    RandomFeatureConfig,
    SGALPConfig,
)
from helper import (
    evaluate_inventory_constraint_threshold,
    gibbs_density_on_grid,
)
from mdp import make_inventory_mdp
from psmd.psmd import PSMD
from self_guided_alp.falp import FALP
from self_guided_alp.sgalp import SelfGuidedALP

INK = "#102A43"
PRIMARY = "#0F6CBD"
TEAL = "#007C83"
ACCENT = "#F59E0B"
MUTED = "#D9E2EC"
DANGER = "#B42318"

plt.rcParams.update({
    "font.family": "sans-serif",
    "axes.titlesize": 12,
    "axes.labelsize": 11,
    "xtick.labelsize": 9,
    "ytick.labelsize": 9,
    "legend.fontsize": 9,
    "axes.spines.top": False,
    "axes.spines.right": False,
})


def _demo_mdp(seed=12345, noise_samples=1000, action_step=0.10):
    config = CONTINUOUS_MDP_NOTEBOOK_CONFIG.inventory.with_updates(
        random_seed=int(seed),
        num_noise_samples=int(noise_samples),
        action_step=float(action_step),
    )
    return make_inventory_mdp(config)


def _violation_surface(beta_1=2.0, beta_2=-2.0, state_points=81, action_points=51, mdp=None):
    mdp = _demo_mdp() if mdp is None else mdp
    state_grid = np.linspace(mdp.lower_state_bound, mdp.upper_state_bound, int(state_points))
    action_grid = np.linspace(0.0, mdp.max_order, int(action_points))
    state_mesh, action_mesh = np.meshgrid(state_grid, action_grid)
    beta = np.asarray([0.0, float(beta_1), float(beta_2)])
    threshold = evaluate_inventory_constraint_threshold(mdp, beta, state_mesh, action_mesh)
    min_index = np.unravel_index(np.argmin(threshold), threshold.shape)
    return SimpleNamespace(
        mdp=mdp,
        state_grid=state_grid,
        action_grid=action_grid,
        state_mesh=state_mesh,
        action_mesh=action_mesh,
        threshold=threshold,
        min_state=float(state_mesh[min_index]),
        min_action=float(action_mesh[min_index]),
        min_value=float(threshold[min_index]),
    )


def plot_violation(beta_1=2.0, beta_2=-2.0, state_points=81, action_points=51):
    data = _violation_surface(beta_1, beta_2, state_points, action_points)
    levels = np.unique(np.quantile(data.threshold, [0.01, 0.05, 0.10, 0.20, 0.35, 0.50, 0.70, 0.85, 0.95]))
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9.4, 3.25), constrained_layout=True)
    image = ax.pcolormesh(data.state_mesh, data.action_mesh, data.threshold, shading="auto", cmap="viridis")
    contour = ax.contour(data.state_mesh, data.action_mesh, data.threshold, levels=levels, colors="white", linewidths=0.65)
    ax.clabel(contour, inline=True, fontsize=9, fmt="%.0f")
    ax.scatter(data.min_state, data.min_action, s=70, color=ACCENT, edgecolor="white", linewidth=1.2,
               label=f"grid minimum = ({data.min_state:.2f}, {data.min_action:.2f})")
    ax.set(xlabel="inventory state  s", ylabel="order quantity  a", xlim=(-4, 12), ylim=(0, 6))
    ax.set_title(rf"Constraint threshold  $f(\beta;s,a)$   |   $\beta_1={beta_1:g}$, $\beta_2={beta_2:g}$")
    ax.legend(loc="lower right")
    cbar = fig.colorbar(image, ax=ax, pad=0.015)
    cbar.set_label(r"$f(\beta;s,a)$")
    plt.show()
    print(f"Most restrictive grid point: s={data.min_state:.3f}, a={data.min_action:.3f}, f={data.min_value:.1f}")


def plot_gibbs(beta_1=2.0, beta_2=-2.0, lambdas=(50.0, 100.0, 200.0)):
    data = _violation_surface(beta_1, beta_2, 81, 51)
    lambda_values = tuple(float(value) for value in lambdas)
    densities = [
        gibbs_density_on_grid(data.threshold, value, data.state_grid, data.action_grid)
        for value in lambda_values
    ]
    common_max = max(float(density.max()) for density in densities)
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, len(lambda_values), figsize=(10.8, 3.1), sharex=True, sharey=True, constrained_layout=True)
    axes = np.atleast_1d(axes)
    image = None
    for ax, value, density in zip(axes, lambda_values, densities):
        image = ax.pcolormesh(data.state_mesh, data.action_mesh, density, shading="auto", cmap="magma",
                              vmin=0.0, vmax=common_max)
        ax.scatter(data.min_state, data.min_action, s=38, color="#FFFFFF", edgecolor=INK, linewidth=0.7)
        ax.set_title(rf"$\lambda={value:g}$")
        ax.set(xlabel="state  s", xlim=(-4, 12), ylim=(0, 6))
    axes[0].set_ylabel("action  a")
    fig.colorbar(image, ax=axes, pad=0.012, label="Gibbs density")
    plt.show()
    concentration = [float(np.max(density)) for density in densities]
    print("Peak density by λ:", {value: round(peak, 4) for value, peak in zip(lambda_values, concentration)})


def plot_constraint_generation_vs_gibbs(beta_1=2.0, beta_2=-2.0, temperature=100.0):
    data = _violation_surface(beta_1, beta_2, 101, 71)
    density = gibbs_density_on_grid(
        data.threshold, float(temperature), data.state_grid, data.action_grid
    )
    mode_index = np.unravel_index(np.argmax(density), density.shape)
    mode_state = float(data.state_mesh[mode_index])
    mode_action = float(data.action_mesh[mode_index])

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10.6, 3.15), sharex=True, sharey=True, constrained_layout=True)
    left = axes[0].pcolormesh(
        data.state_mesh, data.action_mesh, data.threshold, shading="auto", cmap="viridis"
    )
    axes[0].scatter(
        data.min_state, data.min_action, s=70, color=ACCENT, edgecolor="white", linewidth=1.2,
        label="constraint-generation minimizer"
    )
    axes[0].set_title(r"Constraint generation: minimize $f$")
    fig.colorbar(left, ax=axes[0], pad=0.015)

    right = axes[1].pcolormesh(
        data.state_mesh, data.action_mesh, density, shading="auto", cmap="magma"
    )
    axes[1].scatter(
        mode_state, mode_action, s=85, marker="*", color="#FFFFFF", edgecolor=INK, linewidth=0.9,
        label="Gibbs mode"
    )
    axes[1].set_title(rf"Gibbs sampling: maximize $y^*$  ($\lambda={float(temperature):g}$)")
    fig.colorbar(right, ax=axes[1], pad=0.015, label="normalized density")

    for ax in axes:
        ax.set(xlabel="inventory state  s", xlim=(-4, 12), ylim=(0, 6))
        ax.legend(loc="upper right", fontsize=9)
    axes[0].set_ylabel("order quantity  a")
    plt.show()
    print(
        "Same grid point: ",
        f"argmin f = ({data.min_state:.2f}, {data.min_action:.2f}); ",
        f"argmax y* = ({mode_state:.2f}, {mode_action:.2f}).",
        sep="",
    )


def plot_random_feature_examples(seed=17, num_features=5):
    rng = np.random.RandomState(int(seed))
    count = int(np.clip(int(num_features), 1, 24))
    pool_size = 24
    states = np.linspace(-4.0, 12.0, 320)
    z = (states - 4.0) / 8.0

    # Draw a stable pool and use its first N members. Increasing N therefore
    # adds columns without replacing the features already on screen.
    phases = rng.uniform(0.0, 2.0 * np.pi, size=pool_size)
    frequencies = rng.normal(0.0, 2.0, size=pool_size)
    fourier = np.cos(phases[:, None] + frequencies[:, None] * z[None, :])

    relu_bias = rng.normal(0.0, 0.55, size=pool_size)
    relu_slope = rng.normal(0.0, 1.1, size=pool_size)
    relu = np.maximum(0.0, relu_bias[:, None] + relu_slope[:, None] * z[None, :])

    thresholds = rng.uniform(-0.85, 0.85, size=pool_size)
    stumps = (z[None, :] >= thresholds[:, None]).astype(float)

    family_weights = (
        rng.normal(size=pool_size),
        rng.normal(size=pool_size),
        rng.normal(size=pool_size),
    )

    families = (
        (fourier, r"Fourier: $\cos(b_n+w_ns)$"),
        (relu, r"ReLU: $[b_n+w_ns]^+$"),
        (stumps, r"Stump: $\mathbf{1}\{s\geq\tau_n\}$"),
    )
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(10.8, 3.0), sharex=True, constrained_layout=True)
    for ax, (features, title), weights in zip(axes, families, family_weights):
        selected = features[:count]
        approximation = weights[:count] @ selected / np.sqrt(count)
        for feature in selected:
            ax.plot(states, feature, color=PRIMARY, alpha=max(0.08, 0.35 / np.sqrt(count)), linewidth=1.0)
        ax.plot(states, approximation, color=INK, linewidth=2.6, label=rf"VFA draw with $N={count}$")
        ax.axhline(0.0, color=MUTED, linewidth=0.8)
        ax.set(title=f"{title}\nN = {count}", xlabel="inventory state  s", xlim=(-4, 12))
        ax.grid(alpha=0.18)
    axes[0].set_ylabel("feature / approximation value")
    axes[2].legend(loc="best", fontsize=9)
    plt.show()
    print(
        f"Seed {int(seed)}; N={count} nested random features per family "
        "(allowed range 1–24). Fourier is used in Example 6."
    )


def run_psmd_demo(iterations=180, temperature=35.0, seed=777):
    iterations = int(iterations)
    snapshot_iterations = tuple(np.unique(np.linspace(0, iterations, 6, dtype=int)).tolist())
    lower_bound = LowerBoundConfig(
        num_mc_init_states=10,
        chain_length=45,
        burn_in=15,
        proposal_state_std=1.2,
        proposal_action_std=0.9,
        random_seed=int(seed) + 21,
        noise_batch_size=36,
        sampler="metropolis",
        num_walkers=10,
        initial_state=6.0,
    )
    policy = PolicyEvaluationConfig(
        state_grid_size=60,
        policy_noise_batch_size=36,
        policy_noise_seed=int(seed) + 31,
        num_trajectories=12,
        horizon=35,
        simulation_seed=int(seed) + 41,
        initial_state=6.0,
    )
    config = PSMDConfig(
        num_iterations=iterations,
        H=14,
        N=24,
        eval_interval=max(1, iterations // 6),
        step_size=0.20,
        step_size_power=0.5,
        sampler_steps=4,
        proposal_state_std=0.8,
        proposal_action_std=0.8,
        sampling_temperature=float(temperature),
        refresh_fraction=0.10,
        coefficient_clip=5000.0,
        random_seed=int(seed),
        initial_state=6.0,
        snapshot_iterations=snapshot_iterations,
        snapshot_sample_size=60,
        snapshot_sampler_steps=4,
        snapshot_refresh_fraction=0.02,
        lower_bound=lower_bound,
        policy_evaluation=policy,
    )
    mdp = _demo_mdp(seed=int(seed) + 5, noise_samples=72, action_step=0.25)
    model = PSMD(mdp, config=config)
    started = time.time()
    solution = model.run(verbose=False)
    return {
        "model": model,
        "solution": solution,
        "runtime_seconds": time.time() - started,
        "presentation_preset": True,
    }


def plot_psmd_samples(result):
    model = result["model"]
    snapshots = result["solution"]["state_action_snapshots"]
    iterations = [value for value in model.config.snapshot_iterations if value in snapshots]
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, len(iterations), figsize=(11.8, 2.7), sharex=True, sharey=True, constrained_layout=True)
    axes = np.atleast_1d(axes)
    for ax, iteration in zip(axes, iterations):
        snapshot = snapshots[iteration]
        ax.scatter(snapshot["states"], snapshot["actions"], s=14, color=PRIMARY, alpha=0.48, edgecolors="none")
        ax.set_title(f"t = {iteration}")
        ax.set(xlim=(-4.4, 12.4), ylim=(-0.25, 6.25), xlabel="s")
        ax.grid(alpha=0.18)
    axes[0].set_ylabel("a")
    plt.show()
    print(f"Browser run: {model.config.num_iterations} iterations in {result['runtime_seconds']:.1f}s; "
          f"temperature={model.config.sampling_temperature:g}; seed={model.config.random_seed}")


def plot_psmd_bounds(result):
    history = result["solution"]["history"]
    iterations = np.asarray([row["iteration"] for row in history])
    lower = np.asarray([row["lower_bound"] for row in history])
    policy = np.asarray([row["policy_cost"] for row in history])

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9.8, 3.1), constrained_layout=True)
    ax.plot(iterations, lower, "o-", color=PRIMARY, linewidth=2.2, label="estimated lower bound")
    ax.plot(iterations, policy, "o-", color=DANGER, linewidth=2.2, label="simulated greedy-policy cost")
    ax.fill_between(iterations, lower, policy, color=MUTED, alpha=0.38, label="estimated gap")
    ax.set(xlabel="PSMD iteration", ylabel="discounted cost", title="Fixed quadratic VFA  [1, s, s²]")
    ax.legend(fontsize=9)
    ax.grid(alpha=0.22)
    plt.show()
    final_gap = 100.0 * (policy[-1] - lower[-1]) / policy[-1]
    print(f"Estimated gap at the final checkpoint: {final_gap:.1f}%")


def _model_view(mdp, basis, coef, num_features):
    return SimpleNamespace(
        mdp=mdp,
        basis=basis,
        coef=np.asarray(coef, dtype=float),
        num_random_features=int(num_features),
        current_num_random_features=int(num_features),
    )


def run_feature_demo(max_features=6, num_constraints=3000, seed=111):
    max_features = int(max_features)
    num_constraints = int(num_constraints)
    seed = int(seed)
    # The MDP seed and numerical resolution match the executed repository notebook.
    # `seed` controls the nested random-feature family only.
    mdp = _demo_mdp(seed=12345, noise_samples=1000, action_step=0.10)
    random_features = RandomFeatureConfig(bandwidth_choices=(1e-3, 1e-4), random_seed=seed)

    started = time.time()
    falp_models = {}
    for count in range(max_features + 1):
        config = FALPConfig(
            num_random_features=count,
            num_constraints=num_constraints,
            num_state_relevance_samples=num_constraints,
            random_features=random_features,
            solver="scipy",
        )
        model = FALP(mdp, config=config)
        model.fit()
        falp_models[count] = model

    guided_config = SGALPConfig(
        max_random_features=max_features,
        batch_size=1,
        num_constraints=num_constraints,
        num_state_relevance_samples=num_constraints,
        random_features=random_features,
        guiding=GuidingConstraintConfig(
            num_guiding_states=num_constraints,
            allowed_violation=0.0,
            relax_fraction=0.0,
            absolute_floor=0.0,
            retry_scales=(1.0,),
        ),
        solver=HiGHSSolverConfig(method="highs"),
    )
    guided_solver = SelfGuidedALP(mdp, config=guided_config)
    guided_models = {0: falp_models[0]}
    guidance_trace = []
    guided_solver.history = []
    prev_coef = None
    prev_count = None

    # Solve stage by stage so the guide duals are preserved before HiGHS is
    # called again. Those multipliers induce the effective relevance measure.
    for count in guided_solver.stage_feature_counts():
        row = guided_solver.fit_stage(
            num_random_features=count,
            prev_coef=prev_coef,
            prev_num_random_features=prev_count,
        )
        guided_solver.history.append(row)
        guided_solver.coef = np.asarray(row["coef"], dtype=float)
        guided_solver.current_num_random_features = count
        guided_models[count] = _model_view(mdp, guided_solver.basis, row["coef"], count)

        num_falp = int(row["num_falp_constraints"])
        num_guide = int(row["num_guiding_constraints"])
        guide_states = np.asarray([], dtype=float)
        guide_multipliers = np.asarray([], dtype=float)
        if num_guide:
            # The inventory sampler resets to a fixed seed, so this recovers
            # the exact locations used by build_guiding_constraints.
            sampled_states = mdp.sample_state_relevance_states(guided_solver.num_guiding_states)
            guide_states = np.asarray([float(state[0]) for state in sampled_states[:num_guide]])
            marginals = np.asarray(guided_solver.solver_result.ineqlin.marginals, dtype=float)
            guide_multipliers = np.maximum(0.0, -marginals[num_falp:num_falp + num_guide])

        guidance_trace.append({
            "num_features": int(count),
            "guide_states": guide_states,
            "guide_multipliers": guide_multipliers,
        })
        prev_coef = np.asarray(row["coef"], dtype=float)
        prev_count = int(count)

    return {
        "mdp": mdp,
        "falp": falp_models,
        "guided": guided_models,
        "guided_solver": guided_solver,
        "guidance_trace": guidance_trace,
        "feature_counts": list(range(max_features + 1)),
        "runtime_seconds": time.time() - started,
        "num_constraints": num_constraints,
        "seed": seed,
    }


def _values_on_grid(model, grid):
    count = int(getattr(model, "current_num_random_features", getattr(model, "num_random_features")))
    return model.basis.eval_basis_batch(grid, num_random_features=count) @ np.asarray(model.coef)

def _effective_relevance_curve(mdp, guide_states, guide_multipliers, bandwidth=0.65, grid_size=321):
    grid = np.linspace(mdp.lower_state_bound, mdp.upper_state_bound, int(grid_size))
    uniform = np.full_like(grid, 1.0 / (mdp.upper_state_bound - mdp.lower_state_bound))
    states = np.asarray(guide_states, dtype=float).reshape(-1)
    weights = np.asarray(guide_multipliers, dtype=float).reshape(-1)
    active = weights > 1e-9
    states = states[active]
    weights = weights[active]
    dual_mass = float(np.sum(weights))

    if dual_mass == 0.0:
        return grid, uniform, uniform.copy(), states, weights, dual_mass

    bandwidth = max(float(bandwidth), 0.05)
    kernels = np.exp(-0.5 * ((grid[:, None] - states[None, :]) / bandwidth) ** 2)
    kernels /= np.sqrt(2.0 * np.pi) * bandwidth
    kernel_areas = np.trapezoid(kernels, grid, axis=0)
    kernels /= np.maximum(kernel_areas[None, :], 1e-15)
    dual_density = kernels @ weights
    updated = (uniform + dual_density) / (1.0 + dual_mass)
    updated /= np.trapezoid(updated, grid)
    return grid, uniform, updated, states, weights, dual_mass


def plot_state_relevance_updates(result, stage_counts=(2, 3), bandwidth=0.65):
    trace_by_count = {item["num_features"]: item for item in result["guidance_trace"]}
    stage_counts = tuple(int(value) for value in stage_counts)
    missing = [value for value in stage_counts if value not in trace_by_count]
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(f"No guide-dual data are available for N={missing}.")

    records = []
    for count in stage_counts:
        item = trace_by_count[count]
        curve = _effective_relevance_curve(
            result["mdp"], item["guide_states"], item["guide_multipliers"], bandwidth
        )
        records.append((count,) + curve)

    fig, (density_ax, mass_ax) = plt.subplots(
        1, 2, figsize=(10.8, 2.8),
        gridspec_kw={"width_ratios": (2.65, 1.0)}, constrained_layout=True,
    )
    colors = plt.cm.viridis(np.linspace(0.18, 0.92, len(records)))
    grid, uniform = records[0][1], records[0][2]
    density_ax.plot(grid, uniform, color="#526D82", linewidth=1.9, linestyle="--", label=r"original $\nu$: uniform")

    for color, record in zip(colors, records):
        count, grid, _, updated, states, weights, dual_mass = record
        density_ax.plot(grid, updated, color=color, linewidth=2.3, label=rf"after guide at $N={count}$")
        if len(states):
            rug_height = 0.014 * np.sqrt(weights / np.max(weights))
            density_ax.vlines(states, 0.0, rug_height, color=color, alpha=0.38, linewidth=0.8)

    density_ax.set(
        xlabel="inventory state  s", ylabel="effective state-relevance density",
        xlim=(grid[0], grid[-1]), ylim=(0.0, None), title="Effective state relevance",
    )
    density_ax.legend(fontsize=9, loc="best")
    density_ax.grid(alpha=0.20)

    masses = [record[-1] for record in records]
    active_counts = [len(record[-3]) for record in records]
    positions = np.arange(len(records))
    mass_ax.bar(positions, masses, color=colors, width=0.68)
    mass_ax.set(
        xlabel="guided stage", ylabel="total dual mass", title="Update strength",
        xticks=positions, xticklabels=[f"N={count}" for count in stage_counts],
    )
    for position, mass, active_count in zip(positions, masses, active_counts):
        mass_ax.text(position, mass, f"{active_count} active", ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=9)
    mass_ax.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.20)
    plt.show()
    return {"stage_counts": stage_counts, "dual_masses": masses}

def _bound_series(algorithm, seed="mean", best_so_far=False):
    records = FEATURE_BOUND_DATA[algorithm]
    if seed == "mean":
        lower = np.mean([records[key]["lower"] for key in sorted(records)], axis=0)
        upper = np.mean([records[key]["upper"] for key in sorted(records)], axis=0)
    else:
        seed = int(seed)
        if seed not in records:
            raise ValueError(f"seed must be one of {sorted(records)} or 'mean'")
        lower = np.asarray(records[seed]["lower"], dtype=float)
        upper = np.asarray(records[seed]["upper"], dtype=float)
    if best_so_far:
        lower = np.maximum.accumulate(lower)
        upper = np.minimum.accumulate(upper)
    return np.asarray(lower), np.asarray(upper)


def plot_feature_bounds(seed="mean", best_so_far=False):
    counts = np.arange(7)
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10.7, 2.75), sharey=True, constrained_layout=True)
    for ax, algorithm, title in zip(axes, ("falp", "guided"), ("Unguided FALP", "Self-guided ALP")):
        lower, upper = _bound_series(algorithm, seed=seed, best_so_far=best_so_far)
        if seed == "mean":
            records = FEATURE_BOUND_DATA[algorithm]
            offsets = np.linspace(-0.12, 0.12, len(records))
            for offset, key in zip(offsets, sorted(records)):
                seed_lower, seed_upper = _bound_series(algorithm, seed=key, best_so_far=best_so_far)
                ax.scatter(counts + offset, seed_lower, s=13, color=PRIMARY, alpha=0.32)
                ax.scatter(counts + offset, seed_upper, s=13, color=DANGER, alpha=0.32)
        ax.plot(counts, lower, "o-", color=PRIMARY, linewidth=2.4, label="estimated lower bound")
        ax.plot(counts, upper, "o-", color=DANGER, linewidth=2.4, label="simulated policy cost")
        ax.fill_between(counts, lower, upper, color=MUTED, alpha=0.55)
        ax.set(title=title, xlabel="number of random features  N", xticks=counts)
        ax.grid(alpha=0.22)
    axes[0].set_ylabel("discounted cost")
    axes[1].legend(fontsize=9)
    plt.show()
    label = "five-seed mean with individual runs" if seed == "mean" else f"seed {int(seed)}"
    trace = "best-so-far" if best_so_far else "current"
    print(f"Executed notebook output: {label}, {trace} traces. "
          "These are stochastic tutorial estimates, not theorem-level certificates.")
```

<div class="badge">One LP, two infinities</div>

<div class="equation-box compact-equation" style="border-left:8px solid var(--primary)">
<h3><p class="center"><strong>Exact discounted-cost linear program</strong></p></h3>

$$
\begin{aligned}
\max_{V:\,\mathcal{S}\to\mathbb R}\quad
&\int_{\mathcal{S}}V(s)\,\nu(ds)\\
\text{s.t.}\quad
&V(s)\le c(s,a)+\gamma\int_{\mathcal{S}}V(s')\,P(ds'\mid s,a),
\qquad \forall s\in\mathcal{S},\ a\in\mathcal{A}_s.
\end{aligned}
$$

<div class="infinity-tags">
<div class="infinity-tag">$\infty$ constraints: every feasible $(s,a)$</div>
<div class="infinity-tag">$\infty$ columns: the full function $V$</div>
</div>
</div>

<div class="feedback-paths">
<div class="feedback-card constraints">
<h3>1 · Manage the constraint bottleneck</h3>
<div class="feedback-flow">
<span>Construct saddle-point model</span><span class="arrow">→</span>
<span>Optimize</span><span class="arrow">→</span> <span>Refine saddle-point model</span>
</div>
<p class="feedback-method">Constraint violation learning (CVL) uses primal–dual updates to adapt constraint sampling.</p>
</div>
<div class="feedback-card approximation">
<h3>2 · Manage the approximation bottleneck</h3>
<div class="feedback-flow">
<span>Construct value function approximation (VFA) </span><span class="arrow">→</span>
<span>Optimize</span><span class="arrow">→</span>
<span>Refine VFA</span>
</div>
<p class="feedback-method">Self-guided mechanism progressively refines the VFA and the linear program's construction.</p>
</div>
</div>

::: {.notes}
Start from the exact LP: every feasible state–action pair contributes a constraint, while the decision is the full value function. CVL addresses the constraint infinity by holding the basis fixed, constructing the regularized saddle-point model, and jointly optimizing the VFA coefficients and sampling density through PSMD. It has no separate Refine stage. Self-guided ALP addresses the column infinity by constructing random features, optimizing the enriched FALP, and refining with guiding constraints that preserve earlier VFA improvements.
:::

## Approximate Linear Program

<div class="badge">Theory · §4.1</div>

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="38%"}
### ALP Construction
- **Features or basis functions:** features $\varphi_1,\ldots,\varphi_N:\mathcal{S}\mapsto\mathbb{R}$ define the VFA.

- **Weights:** the coefficients $\beta:=(\beta_0,\ldots,\beta_N)\in\mathbb{R}^{N+1}$ define the VFA.

- **One constraint per pair:** every feasible $(s,a)$ contributes a Bellman inequality.

- **Semi-infinite LP:** finitely many coefficients, but infinitely many constraints when states or actions are continuous.
:::

::: {.column width="62%"}
<div class="equation-box compact-equation">
<p class="center"><strong>Finite-dimensional value function approximation (VFA)</strong></p>

$$
V_\beta(s)=\beta_0+\sum_{n=1}^{N}\beta_n\varphi_n(s),
\qquad \beta\in\mathbb R^{N+1}
$$
</div>

<div class="equation-box compact-equation" style="border-left:8px solid var(--accent)">
<p class="center"><strong>Semi-infinite approximate linear program</strong></p>

$$
\begin{aligned}
\max_{\beta\in B}\quad
    & \mathbb E_\nu[V_\beta(s)] \\
\text{s.t.}\quad
    & V_\beta(s) \le c(s,a)
      +\gamma\,\mathbb E[V_\beta(S')\mid s,a], \quad \forall(s,a)\in\mathcal{S}\times\mathcal{A}_s.
\end{aligned}
$$

<p class="center" style="margin:0">$\mathcal{A}_s$ is the feasible action set</p>
</div>
:::
:::

<p class="story-line">Basis functions compress the value function—but not the constraint set.</p>

::: {.notes}
Walk down the three bullets before reading the program. The coefficient vector is finite, but feasibility must hold for every continuous state and every feasible action in the set A. That is the tension driving Section 4: the representation is compact, while finding the important constraints remains difficult.
:::

## Inventory control example {.inventory-slide}

<div class="badge live">Live tutorial · Example 6</div>

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="36%"}
### MDP description:

<div class="definition-list">

<div class="definition-item"><strong>Max backlog:</strong> $4$ units<br> <strong>Max inventory:</strong> $12$ units<br> <strong>Max order quantity:</strong> $6$ units</div>

<div class="definition-item"><strong>State $s\in[-4,12]$</strong> <br> $s>0$ is stock and $s<0$ is backlog.</div>

<div class="definition-item"><strong>Action $a\in \mathcal{A}_s=[0,6]$</strong><br>Order quantity selected before demand is observed.</div>

<div class="definition-item"><strong>Demand $G$</strong><br>$G\sim\operatorname{TN}(6,3.5^2;[0,10])$ is the period's uncertainty.</div>
</div>

<div class="definition-item">
 <strong>Purchase cost:</strong> $20$<br>
 <strong>Holding cost:</strong>  $1$ <br> 
 <strong>Backlog cost:</strong> $25$<br> 
 <strong>Disposal cost:</strong> $5$<br>
 <strong>Lost sales cost:</strong>  $3000$ <br> 
</div>

<p class="tiny muted"><strong>Objective:</strong> minimize expected discounted cost with $\gamma=0.95$.</p>
:::

::: {.column width="64%"}
<div class="equation-box compact-equation">
<p class="center"><strong>Transition after demand</strong></p>

$$
  S'=\min\{\max\{X,-4\},12\}, \qquad X=s+a-G.
$$

<p class="tiny muted center" style="margin:0">Excess above $12$ is disposed; shortage beyond the $-4$ backlog limit becomes lost sales.</p>
</div>

<div class="equation-box compact-equation" style="border-left:8px solid var(--teal)">
<p class="center"><strong>Expected one-period cost</strong></p>

$$
\begin{aligned}
c(s,a)=\mathbb E\big[&20a+(S')^+ +25(-S')^+ +5(X-12)^+ +3000(-4-X)^+\big].
\end{aligned}
$$

<p class="tiny muted center" style="margin:0">purchase + holding + backlog + disposal + lost sales</p>
</div>

<div class="equation-box inventory-alp">
<p class="center"><strong>Quadratic VFA and its inventory ALP</strong></p>

$$
V_\beta(s)=\beta_0+\beta_1s+\beta_2s^2,
\qquad \beta\in B\subseteq\mathbb R^3.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
\max_{\beta\in B}\quad
  &\mathbb E_\nu\!\left[\beta_0+\beta_1s+\beta_2s^2\right] \\
\text{s.t.}\quad
  &\beta_0+\beta_1s+\beta_2s^2 \le c(s,a)+\gamma\,\mathbb E\!\left[
       \beta_0+\beta_1S'+\beta_2(S')^2\mid s,a\right], \quad \forall (s,a)\in[-4,12]\times[0,6].
\end{aligned}
$$

<p class="tiny muted center" style="margin:0">Every feasible pair $(s,a)$ contributes one Bellman inequality.</p>
</div>
:::
:::

<p class="story-line"><strong>Timing:</strong> observe $s$ → order $a$ → demand $G$ arrives → pay cost → carry $S'$ forward.</p>

<p class="source-note">Paper §4.1, Example 6; implementation: <a href="mdp.py">mdp.py</a> and <a href="config.py">config.py</a>.</p>

::: {.notes}
This is a one-item, periodic-review MDP. The state is the inventory position before ordering. The action is an order placed before demand. Demand then creates raw ending inventory X; the nested maximum and minimum enforce the backlog and storage limits to produce the next state. The cost formula attaches a separate economic meaning to each hinge term. The final box substitutes the quadratic VFA into the generic ALP: three coefficients, but one Bellman inequality for every feasible state-action pair.
:::

## Constraint violation function {.violation-slide}

<div class="badge evidence">Paper evidence · Figure 3</div>

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="46%"}
<div class="equation-box compact-equation derivation-box">
<p class="derivation-label"><span class="step-number">1</span>Start from every ALP constraint</p>

$$
V_\beta(s)\le c(s,a)+\gamma\mathbb E[V_\beta(S')\mid s,a],
\qquad \forall(s,a).
$$

<p class="derivation-label"><span class="step-number">2</span>Use the quadratic VFA</p>

$$
V_\beta(s)=\beta_0+\beta_1s+\beta_2s^2.
$$

<p class="derivation-label"><span class="step-number">3</span>Divide by $1-\gamma>0$ and isolate the intercept</p>

$$
\begin{aligned}
(1-\gamma)\beta_0\le{}&c(s,a)
-\beta_1\!\left(s-\gamma\mathbb E[S'\mid s,a]\right)\\[-2pt]
&-\beta_2\!\left(s^2-\gamma\mathbb E[(S')^2\mid s,a]\right).
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\beta_0\le f(\beta;s,a):=
\frac{
\begin{aligned}
c(s,a)&-\beta_1(s-\gamma\mathbb E[S'\mid s,a])\\[-2pt]
&-\beta_2(s^2-\gamma\mathbb E[(S')^2\mid s,a])
\end{aligned}
}{1-\gamma}
$$
</div>
:::

::: {.column width="54%"}
```{pyodide}
#| caption: "Edit β₁ or β₂, then choose Run Code"
#| autorun: true
#| edit: true
#| min-lines: 3
#| max-lines: 4
#| fig-width: 9.4
#| fig-height: 2.75
beta_1 = 2.0
beta_2 = -2.0
plot_violation(beta_1, beta_2, 81, 51)
```
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
Begin with the Bellman inequality that appears once for every feasible state-action pair. Substitute the quadratic value approximation, collect the constant coefficient, and divide by one minus gamma, which is positive. The result shows that each pair imposes an upper threshold f on beta-zero. Darker, smaller values are more restrictive, and a point is violated when beta-zero exceeds that threshold. The orange point is only a grid minimum, not a proof of the continuous global minimum.
:::

## Regularized saddle point problem

<div class="badge">Construct · CVL · equation 10</div>

<div class="equation-box compact-equation" style="border-left:8px solid var(--teal)">
<p class="center"><strong>Define the feasible domain and admissible densities first</strong></p>

$$
D:=\{(s,a):s\in S,\ a\in \mathcal{A}_s\},
\qquad
Y:=\left\{y\ge0:\ y\text{ continuous on }D,\ \int_Dy(s,a)\,d(s,a)=1\right\}.
$$

<!-- <p class="tiny muted center" style="margin:0">Also write $g(\beta):=\sum_{n=1}^N\beta_n\mathbb E_\nu[\varphi_n(S)]$ for the non-intercept part of the ALP objective.</p> -->
</div>

<div class="step-grid">
<div class="step-card">
<p class="derivation-label"><span class="step-number">1</span>Eliminate the intercept</p>

$$
\beta_0^* =\min_{(s,a)\in D}f(\beta;s,a),
$$

$$
F=\max_{\beta\in B}\left\{\min_D f(\beta;s,a)+\sum_{n=1}^N\beta_n\mathbb E_\nu[\varphi_n(s)]\right\}.
$$
</div>

<div class="step-card">
<p class="derivation-label"><span class="step-number">2</span>Lift the search to $Y$</p>

$$
\min_{(s,a)\in D}f(\beta;s,a)
=\inf_{y\in Y}\mathbb E_y[f(\beta;s,a)].
$$

<p class="muted">An average cannot beat the minimum; concentrating densities approach it.</p>
</div>

<div class="step-card">
<p class="derivation-label"><span class="step-number">3</span>Regularize the density</p>

$$
\mathbb E_y[f(\beta;s,a)]+\lambda D_{\mathrm{KL}}(y\Vert p_u)
$$

<p class="muted">The uniform reference $p_u$ discourages collapse onto a single pair.</p>
</div>
</div>

<div class="equation-box compact-equation" style="border-left:8px solid var(--accent)">
$$
\boxed{
F(\lambda)=\max_{\beta\in B}\min_{y\in Y}
\left\{\mathbb E_y[f(\beta;s,a)]
+\lambda D_{\mathrm{KL}}(y\Vert p_u)+\sum_{n=1}^N\beta_n\mathbb E_\nu[\varphi_n(s)]\right\}.}
$$
</div>

<p class="story-line"><strong>Construct step:</strong> replace nonconvex separation by optimization over a smooth, sampleable density.</p>

::: {.notes}
Define the domain D and density set Y before using either. Step one eliminates the intercept because the ALP objective increases in beta-zero. Step two lifts the nonconvex point search to a linear expectation over densities without changing its value. Step three adds KL regularization relative to the uniform density. This is the construct step of CVL: it builds a sampleable alternative to repeatedly solving the global separation problem.
:::

## The optimal density is Gibbs

<div class="badge">Theoretical result · Proposition 2</div>

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="61%"}
<div class="theorem-box">
<p class="center"><strong>Fix $\beta\in B$ and $\lambda>0$</strong></p>

$$
\min_{y\in Y}
\left\{\mathbb E_y[f(\beta;s,a)]
+\lambda D_{\mathrm{KL}}(y\Vert p_u)\right\}
$$

<p class="center"><strong>The minimum is attained at</strong></p>

$$
\boxed{
y^*_{\lambda,\beta}(s,a)=
\frac{\exp[-f(\beta;s,a)/\lambda]}
    {\displaystyle\int_D\exp[-f(\beta;s',a')/\lambda]\,d(s',a')}
}
$$
</div>

<p class="tiny muted center" style="margin-top:0.25rem">The uniform reference density $p_u$ cancels between numerator and denominator.</p>
:::

::: {.column width="39%"}
### Key observations

<!-- <div class="equation-box compact-equation">
The stationarity condition for the density and the normalization multiplier $\eta$ is

$$
f+\lambda\!\left(\log\frac{y}{p_u}+1\right)+\eta=0.
$$

Thus $y\propto p_u\exp(-f/\lambda)$; normalization gives equation (11).
</div> -->

::: {.compact-list}
- KL strict convexity identifies the inner minimizer.
- Smaller $\lambda$ sharpens mass around minimizers of $f$.
- Metropolis–Hastings needs only relative density values.
:::
:::
:::

<p class="story-line"><strong>The construct step now has a closed-form target density that can be sampled.</strong></p>

::: {.notes}
This is the theoretical bridge from the regularized saddle problem to a practical sampler. For fixed coefficients and positive lambda, the KL-regularized inner problem attains its optimum at the normalized Gibbs density. The first-order stationarity condition gives the exponential form, and the integral enforces unit mass. Because Metropolis-Hastings uses density ratios, the normalizing integral need not be computed explicitly.
:::

## Same target, different search {.cg-slide}

<div class="badge">Constraint generation versus CVL</div>

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="35%"}
### Hold $\beta$ fixed

<div class="equation-box compact-equation">
<p class="tiny muted center"><strong>Exact separation</strong></p>

$$
\begin{aligned}
(s_{\mathrm{CG}},a_{\mathrm{CG}})
&\in\arg\min_{(s,a)\in D}\{f(\beta;s,a)-\beta_0\}\\
&=\arg\min_{(s,a)\in D}f(\beta;s,a).
\end{aligned}
$$

<p class="tiny muted center"><strong>Gibbs mode</strong></p>

$$
\boxed{\arg\max_D y^*_{\lambda,\beta}
=\arg\min_D f(\beta;s,a).}
$$
</div>

::: {.compact-list}
- Constraint generation returns one worst pair.
- CVL samples a neighborhood around the same target.
- The identity holds for fixed $\beta$ and every $\lambda>0$.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="65%"}
```{pyodide}
#| caption: "Change β or λ; the two markers remain aligned"
#| autorun: true
#| edit: true
#| min-lines: 3
#| max-lines: 4
#| fig-width: 10.6
#| fig-height: 3.15
beta_1, beta_2 = 2.0, -2.0
temperature = 100.0
plot_constraint_generation_vs_gibbs(beta_1, beta_2, temperature)
```
:::
:::

<p class="story-line"><strong>Constraint generation searches for the mode; CVL turns that target into a sampling distribution.</strong></p>

::: {.notes}
This comparison is pointwise in beta. Exact separation minimizes f minus beta-zero, which has the same minimizers as f. Because the Gibbs exponential decreases strictly with f, its modes are exactly the minimizers of f. The methods do not follow the same coefficient trajectory: constraint generation adds one worst constraint, whereas CVL samples informative constraints around the same target region.
:::

## PSMD updates coefficients and density

<div class="badge">Optimize · PSMD Algorithm 1</div>

<div class="algorithm-grid">
<div class="algorithm-step">
<p class="derivation-label"><span class="step-number">1</span>Initialize and sample</p>

$$
\beta^{(0)}=0,\quad y^{(0)}=p_u,\qquad
(\widehat s_t,\widehat a_t)\sim y^{(t)},\quad
\check s_t\sim P(\cdot\mid\widehat s_t,\widehat a_t).
$$

<p>The current density chooses the state–action constraint; the transition model supplies the next-state sample.</p>
</div>

<div class="algorithm-step">
<p class="derivation-label"><span class="step-number">2</span>Estimate the primal gradient</p>

$$
\widehat L_t(\beta)=
\frac{c(\widehat s_t,\widehat a_t)
-\sum_{n=1}^N\beta_n[\varphi_n(\widehat s_t)-\gamma\varphi_n(\check s_t)]}
{1-\gamma}
+\sum_{n=1}^N\beta_n\mathbb E_\nu[\varphi_n(S)],
$$

$$
\widehat g_t=\nabla_\beta\widehat L_t(\beta^{(t)}).
$$
</div>

<div class="algorithm-step">
<p class="derivation-label"><span class="step-number">3</span>Euclidean ascent for $\beta$</p>

$$
\boxed{\beta^{(t+1)}
=\Pi_B\!\left(\beta^{(t)}+\eta_t\widehat g_t\right).}
$$

<p>The maximizing variable updates the VFA coefficients and is projected back onto the compact set $B$.</p>
</div>

<div class="algorithm-step">
<p class="derivation-label"><span class="step-number">4</span>KL mirror descent for $y$</p>

$$
\boxed{
y^{(t+1)}(s,a)\propto
[y^{(t)}(s,a)]^{\frac{1}{1+\eta_t\lambda_t}}
\exp\!\left[
-\frac{\eta_t\widehat f_t(\beta^{(t)};s,a)}
{1+\eta_t\lambda_t}\right].}
$$

<p>Decrease $\eta_t$ and $\lambda_t$ at order $1/\sqrt{t}$, then form weighted averages $\bar\beta$ and $\bar y$.</p>
</div>
</div>

<p class="story-line"><strong>Output:</strong> use the greedy cost-minimizing policy induced by $V(\cdot;\bar\beta)$.</p>

::: {.notes}
PSMD is primal-dual stochastic mirror descent on the regularized saddle problem. It draws a state-action pair from the current density and a next state from the transition law, giving unbiased first-order information for the maximizing coefficient vector. Beta uses Euclidean projected ascent. The minimizing density uses a KL mirror step, and both the step size and regularization parameter decrease at order one over square root t. The algorithm returns a weighted average coefficient vector and its greedy policy.
:::

## Value function approximation via random features {.random-feature-slide}

<div class="badge">Construct · §4.3</div>

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
<div class="equation-box compact-equation">
<p class="center"><strong>So far: fixed basis functions</strong></p>

$$
\boldsymbol{\phi}(s)=\bigl(1,s,s^2\bigr), \qquad V_{\beta}(s)=\beta_0+\beta_1s+\beta_2s^2.
$$
</div>
:::

::: {.column width="40%"}
<div class="equation-box compact-equation">
<p class="center"><strong>Next: random features</strong></p>

$$
\theta_n\overset{iid}{\sim}\vartheta,\qquad
\varphi_n(s)=\phi\!\left(\theta_n^\top(1,s)\right), \qquad V_N(s;\beta)=\beta_0+\sum_{n=1}^N\beta_n\varphi_n(s).
$$
</div>
:::
:::

```{pyodide}
#| caption: "Change the seed or the number of random features"
#| autorun: true
#| edit: true
#| min-lines: 3
#| max-lines: 4
#| fig-width: 10.8
#| fig-height: 3.0
seed = 17
num_features = 1  # try 1, 5, or 12
plot_random_feature_examples(seed, num_features)
```

<p class="story-line"><strong>Each draw creates a fixed nonlinear basis; the ALP chooses its linear combination.</strong></p>


::: {.notes}
Contrast the fixed quadratic basis used in the inventory example with the random-feature approximation. Random features separate construction from fitting: their nonlinear parameters are sampled once from a prescribed distribution, and only their linear weights are decision variables. The three plots show Fourier, ReLU, and stump examples; change the number of features to see how the available approximation shapes become richer.
:::

## Feature-based ALP with continuous constraints

<div class="badge">Construct + optimize · FALP</div>

<div class="step-grid">
<div class="step-card">
<p class="derivation-label"><span class="step-number">1</span>Draw columns</p>
<p>Draw $\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_N\sim\vartheta$ and fix the random features $\varphi_n$.</p>
</div>
<div class="step-card">
<p class="derivation-label"><span class="step-number">2</span>Generate the VFA</p>
$$
V_N(s;\beta)=\beta_0+\sum_{n=1}^N\beta_n\varphi_n(s).
$$
</div>
<div class="step-card">
<p class="derivation-label"><span class="step-number">3</span>Keep every row</p>
<p>Impose one Bellman inequality for every feasible continuous pair $(s,a)$.</p>
</div>
</div>

<div class="equation-box compact-equation" style="border-left:8px solid var(--primary)">
<p class="center"><strong>FALP$_N$: random columns, continuous constraint set</strong></p>

$$
\begin{aligned}
\max_{\beta\in\mathbb R^{N+1}}\quad
&\mathbb E_{\nu}[V_N(S;\beta)]\\
\text{s.t.}\quad
&V_N(s;\beta)
\le c(s,a)+\gamma\,\mathbb E[V_N(S';\beta)\mid s,a], \qquad \forall s\in\mathcal{S},\ a\in\mathcal{A}_s.
\end{aligned}
$$
</div>

<div class="theorem-box">
<p class="center"><strong>Key convergence result:</strong></p>
<p class="center">Since we have $V_N\le V^*$, the FALP optimal objective value $\mathbb E_{\nu}[V_N]$ is a valid lower bound on the optimal policy cost $\mathbb E_{\nu}[V^*]$.</p>

$$
0\le \mathbb E_{\nu}[V^*]-\mathbb E_{\nu}[V_N] \le \lVert V^*-V_N\rVert_{1,\nu} \le O(\frac{1}{\sqrt{N}})
$$

<p class="small center">Under some regularity and universal-feature assumptions, this convergence holds with high probability.</p>
</div>

<p class="story-line"><strong>Randomness enters through the columns $\theta_n$; the Bellman constraints still cover every state–action pair.</strong> In the inventory run, $\nu$ is uniform.</p>

::: {.notes}
FALP samples basis parameters, not Bellman constraints. Once the feature draw is fixed, the model is linear in beta, but it remains semi-infinite: the Bellman inequality must hold for every feasible state-action pair. The repository uses constraint sampling only as an implementation device; that numerical approximation is not part of the FALP definition on this slide.
:::

## FALP policy convergence caveat

<div class="cards">
<div class="card">
<h3>What FALP controls</h3>

$$
\lVert V^*-V_N\rVert_{1,\nu}
\longrightarrow 0.
$$

<p>A global approximation guarantee averaged under $\nu$.</p>
</div>

<div class="card teal">
<h3>What the policy uses</h3>

$$
\begin{aligned}
\pi^*(s)&\in\arg\min_{a\in\mathcal A_s}
\left\{c(s,a)+\gamma\mathbb E[V^*(S')\mid s,a]\right\}\\
\pi_N(s)&\in\arg\min_{a\in\mathcal A_s}
\left\{c(s,a)+\gamma\mathbb E[V_N(S')\mid s,a]\right\}.
\end{aligned}
$$

<p>A local ranking of actions at each inventory state.</p>
</div>
</div>


<div class="cor-strip">
<span><strong>Improvement:</strong> $\lVert V^*-V_N\rVert_{1,\nu} \ge  \lVert V^*-V_{N+1}\rVert_{1,\nu}$ </span><span class="arrow">$\quad\nRightarrow\quad$</span>
<span><strong>Not guaranteed:</strong> $\mathrm{PV}_\chi(\pi_{N+1})\le \mathrm{PV}_\chi(\pi_N)$</span>
</div>

<p class="story-line"><strong>The FALP results ensure VFA and lower bouund improvements, but not monotone improvement of the greedy-policy upper bound.</strong></p>

::: {.notes}
This is a mechanism, not a numerical claim about a particular random-feature draw. In the inventory problem, the greedy policy compares order quantities through their one-step cost plus approximate continuation value. Near a reorder threshold, the best two actions have a small true action gap. Even when the FALP objective and the value approximation converge on average under the state-relevance distribution, localized continuation-value errors can change the sign of that gap and move the threshold. Thus the exact policy cost $J_\nu(\pi_N)$ is an upper bound for this cost-minimization problem, but the FALP convergence theorem alone does not make those upper bounds monotone. This does not say the policies can never converge; it says that lower-bound convergence by itself is insufficient.
:::

## Self-guided ALP

<div class="badge">Construct + optimize + refine · equation 12</div>

<div class="cor-strip">
<span><strong>Construct:</strong> add $B$ features</span><span class="arrow">→</span>
<span><strong>Optimize:</strong> solve FALP$_N$</span><span class="arrow">→</span>
<span><strong>Refine:</strong> retain the statewise floor</span><span class="arrow">↺</span>
</div>

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="60%"}
<div class="equation-box compact-equation">
<p class="center"><strong>At round $q$, $N=qB$ and the previous VFA becomes a guide</strong></p>

$$
\begin{aligned}
\max_{\beta\in\mathbb R^{N+1}}\quad
&\mathbb E_{\nu}[V_N(S;\beta)]\\
\text{s.t.}\quad
&V_N(s;\beta)\le c(s,a)+\gamma\mathbb E[V_N(S';\beta)\mid s,a],
\quad\forall s\in\mathcal{S},\ a\in\mathcal{A}_s,\\
&\boxed{V_N(s;\beta)\ge
V_{N-B}(s;\beta^{\mathrm{SG}}_{N-B}),\quad\forall s\in\mathcal{S}.}
\end{aligned}
$$
</div>
:::

::: {.column width="40%"}
### Why the guide matters

::: {.compact-list}
- **Memory:** the new lower bound cannot fall below the previous one.
- **Signal:** a dual multiplier $y_N^*(s)$ can be positive only where the guide binds.
- **Reweighting:** those shadow prices induce an effective objective distribution.
:::

<div class="equation-box compact-equation" style="border-left:8px solid var(--teal)">
<p class="center"><strong>Equivalent state relevance after the solve</strong></p>

$$
\nu'_N(s)=
\frac{\nu(s)+y_N^*(s)}
{1+\int_{\mathcal{S}}y_N^*(u)\,du}.
$$
</div>
:::
:::

<div class="cor-strip">
<span><strong>Self-guided ALP improves </strong> $\lVert V^*-V_N\rVert_{1,\nu} \ge  \lVert V^*-V_{N+1}\rVert_{1,\nu}$
<span><strong>only if</strong> $\lVert V^*-V_N\rVert_{\infty} \ge  \lVert V^*-V_{N+1}\rVert_{\infty}$</span>
</div>

<p class="story-line"><strong>Self-guided ALP guarantees improving worst-case policy performance from $N$ to $N+1$</strong></p>

::: {.notes}
This is the complete construct–optimize–refine loop. Construct samples a new batch of columns. Optimize solves the enriched FALP. Refine carries the earlier VFA forward as a statewise floor. Appending zero coefficients preserves the previous feasible solution. The dual interpretation is ex post: the self-guided optimum is equivalent to a FALP whose state-relevance distribution is the normalized sum of the original distribution and the guiding-constraint dual density. Complementarity means extra weight can occur only where the guide is tight.
:::
